scene_description: A small tiled bedroom with a foreground bed, white shelving and a narrow cabinet against the back wall, two floor lamps, a partly open paneled door, and a white furniture panel at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial image shows only a thin pale vertical strip beside the dark doorway, without the broad visible door leaf that projects into the room in the reference. The right foreground white panel occupies much less of the view than in the reference.
candidate_target_observations: A broad pale paneled door leaf is now visible at the right of the doorway, but it is near the back wall and is cropped at the top, rather than projecting diagonally across the center-right foreground as in the reference. The right white panel remains visible, though its occlusion and silhouette differ from the reference.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The candidate's shelf, cabinet, lamps and bed read as recognizable room furnishings. The door appears as a substantial paneled leaf, but its visible placement and angle do not reproduce the reference's strong central foreground occlusion; its upper connection is outside the frame. RGB views do not establish physical contact or collisions.
new_visible_defects: The candidate's door is cut off by the top edge and presents a relatively narrow, nearly upright silhouette at the far right compared with the prominent angled reference door. The cabinet's upper front appears more open and skeletal than the reference's framed glass-front appearance.
other_changes: The candidate shows a shifted, closer composition: the bed is larger in the foreground and the right panel is more prominent than initially. A pale floor patch is visible near the bed, but the reference has more varied tan and dark floor texture. Candidate surfaces and lighting remain smoother and cooler than the reference, whose lamps cast warmer, more pronounced light pools. The reference also shows pale wood grain on the door, largely absent from the candidate.

evidence.description: Broad wood-grained door leaf projects diagonally into the center-right of the room and occludes the background.
Dark doorway with only a narrow pale strip at its right edge; no comparably broad projecting door leaf is visible.
Pale paneled door leaf is visible near the back right but is top-cropped and does not extend into the center foreground like the reference.
Large white foreground furniture panel partly occludes the right side of the room.
White panel occupies the right foreground, with a different outline and relationship to the door.
White shelves, narrow cabinet, and two floor lamps remain recognizable, though surfaces are simplified.
Warm lamp illumination and varied tan floor appearance contrast with the smoother candidate rendering.

uncertainty: The intended target was not explicitly specified; the door leaf and its foreground occlusion are assessed as the most salient bedroom-specific change. Different framing makes exact spatial comparison uncertain, and hidden geometry and physical contact cannot be determined from these images.
